title: X0XReport
description: Panopticon's catalog-gap report: the <DOM>-X0X fallback and ZZZ-X0X domainless findings from a review, emitted as candidate records for OCRDb's new-code adjudication pool. A candidate maps onto the OCRDb entry model (name / default_severity / cwe / examples / recurrence) plus a `rationale` — why no existing code fit — which is the load-bearing signal for deciding whether to mint a new code. Basic schema only; NOT wired into synthesize yet (emission + occurrence clustering + evidence scrubbing land in 5.1). `additionalProperties` is left open on every object: this is a young contract meant to grow without a schema bump.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS report schema, bumped only on a breaking shape change.

generated_by.description: Provenance of the Panopticon run that emitted this report.

ocrdb_version.description: The OCRDb bundle version the review ran against. Every candidate is a gap RELATIVE to this catalog state, so it can be re-evaluated (or retired) as the catalog grows.

target.description: What was reviewed. Optional, and may be scrubbed before a candidate leaves Panopticon (a 5.1 policy decision).

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the report was produced (optional).

candidates.description: One record per proposed OCRDb code candidate — a catalog gap with its supporting evidence.

domain.description: The OCRDb domain the candidate belongs to, or `ZZZ` when even the domain could not be derived (the domainless sentinel).

fallback_code.description: The `<DOM>-X0X` (or `ZZZ-X0X`) fallback code Panopticon assigned during the review — ties the candidate back to its source finding.

proposed_name.description: Panopticon's suggested kebab-case anti-pattern name (e.g. `unbounded-external-response-read`). Maps to the OCRDb entry `name`; the adjudicator finalizes it.

summary.description: The anti-pattern in one human-readable line — becomes an OCRDb `examples` entry.

description.description: What the pattern is and why it is a defect.

severity.description: Proposed default severity — maps to OCRDb `default_severity`.

area.description: The OCRDb sub-grouping (domain `area`) the candidate would slot into, if known.

rationale.description: WHY no existing OCRDb code matched — the catalog-gap justification. The load-bearing field for adjudication: the argument for minting a new code rather than reusing one.

recurrence.description: How many times this pattern was seen (a convenience mirror of len(occurrences); OCRDb tracks `recurrence`).

occurrences.description: The concrete evidence sites for this candidate. A naive emitter produces one occurrence per finding; a clustering emitter (5.1) aggregates many under one candidate.

snippet.description: Optional code excerpt. Whether it is populated (and scrubbed of secrets / PII) is a wiring/policy decision deferred to 5.1.

finding_id.description: The Panopticon finding id this occurrence came from — traces the candidate back to the source review report.
